clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-677 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8524-exemption-j-brent-clarke-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed August 26, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), exempts J. Brent Clarke from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. First end: the order's own stated end, September 30, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of September 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when September 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8866, signed August 22, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("by Executive Order No. 8524 of August 26, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending September 30, 1942". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing.

savings.reason: The exemption let J. Brent Clarke remain in service past the retirement age that would otherwise have required automatic separation; service rendered while the exemption ran is an accrued effect that remains after the stated end date. The order says nothing about any status, right or duty after September 30, 1941, so no independent continuing command or residual obligation of this order survives its stated term. Later service under the further exemption came from a separate order, not from this one.
